$comment: CURATED. Not generated, not fetched, and not derived from any statistic.
WHERE THIS CAME FROM. The list was proposed by an agent on 2026-09-01 from
established Commander deckbuilding practice, and every name in it was then
checked against this project's own corpus by exact string on the same day
(all 27 resolved, all commander-legal). It is an OPINION with an owner, not
a measurement, and it is stated that way on purpose: ADR-0008 forbids
querying EDHREC, and the inclusion statistic the product could otherwise
have leaned on is inert in production (`stats: null`), so `w.inclusion`
contributes exactly zero. There is no number behind 'staple' available to
this codebase. A curated list is honest about being an opinion; a list that
wore a percentage it did not measure would not be.
WHO DECIDES. The repository owner. This file is meant to be edited — adding
a name, deleting one you disagree with, or rewriting `why` are all ordinary
changes and need no code change. Update `curatedAt` when you do.
THE INCLUSION PRINCIPLE, and it is deliberately narrow. A card belongs here
only if BOTH hold:
1. it does a job EVERY Commander deck has — accelerate, fix, draw, answer
a permanent, answer a board, protect the commander; and
2. inside the colours that can cast it, it is the DEFAULT answer to that
job at its cost, so a deck of those colours that leaves it out is
making a deliberate choice rather than a neutral one.
It is NOT 'good cards' and NOT 'expensive cards'. A five-hundred-card
staples list is a synonym for 'good cards' and says nothing; the value of
this list is entirely in what it refuses. Twenty-seven entries is small
enough that a reader can disagree with it card by card, which is the only
form of accountability an opinion can have.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Colour-pair fixing lands — shocks, fetches,
duals, triomes, the Castle cycle. Each is a staple of the two or three
colours it serves, and putting them here would add sixty entries that are
wrong for most decks and turn the list into a mana base. The mana base is
its own tool (doc 05 s5.2). Only lands that fix for ANY deck are here.
Also absent: cards whose case rests on a theme (tribal, tokens, graveyard).
Those are what synergy and semantic emphasis are for.
THERE IS NO `type` FIELD, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The product splits this
list into 'staples' and 'staple lands' — see `staples.ts`, which partitions
it by the card's OWN type line out of the corpus. Whether a card is a land
is a fact the database already holds; a hand-typed copy of it here could
disagree with the database, and two functions of the same data disagreeing
is precisely the defect ADR-0031 was written about. The split the user
asked for is real; the second copy of the answer is what was rejected.
`why` IS PROSE FOR THE OWNER AND IS READ BY NO CODE. Only `name` is loaded.
It is here so a reviewer can audit the principle entry by entry rather than
trusting the list as a block. It is written as a job, not as a role name,
so it cannot be mistaken for a second copy of the corpus's `primary_role`.

cards.name: Sol Ring
cards.why: Two mana on turn one for one mana. No deck declines it.

cards.name: Arcane Signet
cards.why: Two-mana rock that taps for any colour your commander is.

cards.name: Lightning Greaves
cards.why: Every deck has a commander, and every commander gets killed.

cards.name: Command Tower
cards.why: Taps for your whole identity, costs nothing, in any deck.

cards.name: Exotic Orchard
cards.why: Free fixing off the table in any multicolour game.

cards.name: Evolving Wilds
cards.why: Fixing for a colour you are missing, at no colour cost.

cards.name: Terramorphic Expanse
cards.why: The second copy of Evolving Wilds; decks run both.

cards.name: Myriad Landscape
cards.why: A land that ramps, playable in every colour combination.

cards.name: Swords to Plowshares
cards.why: White's cheapest unconditional answer to a creature.

cards.name: Path to Exile
cards.why: The second copy of Swords; white decks want both.

cards.name: Generous Gift
cards.why: White's answer to anything at all, not only creatures.

cards.name: Wrath of God
cards.why: The board wipe every white deck is expected to hold.

cards.name: Counterspell
cards.why: Blue's baseline answer to a spell, at the baseline price.

cards.name: Pongify
cards.why: Blue's one-mana answer to a creature it cannot counter.

cards.name: Rhystic Study
cards.why: Blue's default draw engine in a four-player game.

cards.name: Cyclonic Rift
cards.why: Blue's answer to a board it has already lost.

cards.name: Demonic Tutor
cards.why: Black's baseline: any card, two mana, no condition.

cards.name: Toxic Deluge
cards.why: Black's board wipe that scales to any board.

cards.name: Feed the Swarm
cards.why: Black's only cheap answer to an enchantment.

cards.name: Chaos Warp
cards.why: Red's only answer to a permanent it otherwise cannot touch.

cards.name: Blasphemous Act
cards.why: Red's board wipe; costs one mana in the games that need it.

cards.name: Vandalblast
cards.why: Red's answer to the artifacts every other deck is ramping on.

cards.name: Cultivate
cards.why: Green's baseline ramp: a land in play and a land in hand.

cards.name: Kodama's Reach
cards.why: The second copy of Cultivate; green decks run both.

cards.name: Beast Within
cards.why: Green's answer to any permanent, which green otherwise lacks.

cards.name: Nature's Claim
cards.why: Green's one-mana answer to an artifact or enchantment.

cards.name: Sylvan Library
cards.why: Green's default draw, and it fixes green's flood problem.
